citation.title: Evolutionary de-homogenization using a generative model for optimizing solid-porous infill structures considering the stress concentration issue
citation.authors: Shuzhi Xu, Hiroki Kawabe, Kentaro Yaji

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Against traditional single-material Stress-TO, low-fidelity optimization lowers maximum stress by 13% at a 13% target volume fraction and 9.7% at an 18% target.
claim.alternatives: Conclusion item 5 qualitatively says low-fidelity optimization has performance advantages over traditional single-material stress optimization, amplified when used to initialize MFTD.

baseline.classical_method: Traditional single-material stress-based topology optimization (Stress-TO); low-fidelity method also compared with MFTD
baseline.problem_size: 2D; mesh resolution not stated for primary comparison
baseline.quality_metric: Maximum von Mises stress and volume fraction
baseline.quality_gap: Section 4.5, Fig. 19: maximum stress reductions of 13% and 9.7% at target volume fractions 13% and 18%, respectively; reported volume fractions are 13.12% vs 13.74% and 17.89% vs 18.11%.

R1.evidence: Conclusion: the primary comparison is design quality; no speed comparison is made.

R2.evidence: Sections 4.5–4.6: no solver efficiency, hardware mismatch, iteration excess, or per-iteration baseline comparison established.

R3.evidence: Conclusion: no speed claim is made.

R4.evidence: Sections 4.5–4.6 and Figs. 19, 21: detailed CAD designs are evaluated with high-fidelity finite-element stress analysis and volume fractions, but failed or infeasible designs are not counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: Several numerical cases; counts not stated (Sections 4.1–4.6).
